pages.ja:
……間桐臓硯は、以前と変わらぬ姿で立っていた。
アーチャーに断たれた半身も健在だ。
死を待つだけだった老魔術師は、あの夜の出来事が幻だったかのように笑っている。

pages.en:
…Zouken Matou stands before me, unchanged from the last time I saw him.

Even the half of his body severed by Archer has been restored.

The ancient mage who lay waiting for death smiles as though the events of that night were an illusion.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Matou Zouken is standing there, his figure just like before.
His body, which Archer sliced in two before my eyes, is whole once more.
The old magus that could only wait for death is laughing, as if that event was an illusion.

pages.ja:
その理由は不明だが、本当にあの状態から持ち直したというのなら、それは治癒ではなく復元の域だ。
傷を治す、というレベルの話じゃない。
無くなった肉体、失われた肉体を元に戻す大魔術だ。
なら
それは、不死身と呼ばれるものではないのか。

pages.en:
I do not know what magecraft made this possible. But if he truly recovered from such a condition, it lies beyond healing and approaches restoration.

This is not a matter of closing wounds.

It is great magecraft capable of returning flesh that has ceased to exist.

Would that not make him effectively invulnerable?
pages.mirrorMoon:
I don’t know how he did it, but if he really did recover from that state, it’s more on a level of restoration than recovery.
It’s not just healing a wound.
It takes great magic to restore a piece of one’s body that has been lost.
Then
isn’t this called immortality?

」

pages.en:
“Now then. What do you intend to accomplish with that little stick, boy?”

“——”

I stand frozen with the Reinforced temple admonition stick pointed at Zouken.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well. What do you intend with a single piece of wood, child?”
“
”
I stand there while pointing the strengthened stick at Zouken.

pages.ja:
臓硯に踏み込む為の前進も、セイバーを追いかける為の後退もできない。
……臓硯が不死身だとしたら、確かに、こんな棒切れ一本でどうにかできる相手じゃない

pages.en:
I can neither advance to attack him nor retreat to follow Saber.

…If Zouken is immortal, then he is certainly no opponent I can overcome with a single wooden rod.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I can’t charge at Zouken, nor can I retreat to follow Saber.
…If Zouken is immortal, a scrap of wood will never be able to match him

pages.ja:
「ワシを仕留めるか、サーヴァントの後を追うか。どちらにせよ、足を動かさねば始まるまいて」
そう語る老魔術師の周囲には、キイキイと蠢くものがある。
いや、蠢いているのは臓硯の周りだけではない。
暗い影、月光を遮断する闇そのものが移動している。
pages.jaRuby:
「ワシを仕留めるか、サーヴァントの後を追うか。どちらにせよ、足を動かさねば始まるまいて」

pages.en:
“Will you attempt to finish me, or pursue your Servant? Whichever you choose, nothing will begin until you move your feet.”

Things squeal and writhe around the old mage as he speaks.

No. They do not move only around Zouken.

Dark shadows—the darkness itself, which shuts out the moonlight—is in motion.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Will you try to kill me, or will you go after your Servant? Either way, nothing starts until you move.”
Something is squirming around the old magus as he speaks.
No, it’s not just his surroundings.
The darkness itself is moving, blocking the moonlight.

pages.ja:
「
虫」
見えなくとも判る。
闇の正体は細かく、おぞましいほど密集した虫の群だ。
このお堂の四隅、壁という壁に、闇より黒いモノが敷き詰められている。
この空間は、ガサガサと壁を這う虫の音と、肉の腐った臭いで支配されていた。
pages.jaRuby:
「
虫」

pages.en:
“—Insects.”

I know without seeing them.

The darkness is an immense swarm of tiny insects, packed together with nauseating density.

Every corner and every wall of the temple hall is carpeted with something blacker than darkness.

The dry scraping of insects crawling over the walls and the stench of rotting flesh rule this place.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Worms.”
I can tell, even though I can’t see them.
The darkness is probably swarms of worms.
The walls of this temple are covered in something darker than darkness itself.
This space is filled with the sound of creeping worms and the smell of rotten meat.

pages.ja: 「どうした、なにを躊躇う？ 先日、ワシの腹を断ってくれたのはおぬしたちであろう。遠坂の小娘と組んで、ワシを始末する腹ではなかったのか？」
pages.jaRuby: 「どうした、なにを躊躇う？ 先日、ワシの腹を断ってくれたのはおぬしたちであろう。遠坂の小娘と組んで、ワシを始末する腹ではなかったのか？」
pages.en: “Why do you hesitate? It was you and your companions who opened my belly the other night. After joining with the Tohsaka girl, did you not mean to dispose of me?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Why do you hesitate? Your little alliance cut me in half only yesterday. Did you not cooperate with Tohsaka specifically to kill me?”

pages.ja:
……蟲遣いは明らかに愉しんでいる。
警策一本で、部屋中に集まった何万という虫を払う事などできない。
臓硯が号令を下せば、何をやっても虫の波に飲まれるだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
……[ruby text=ぞうけん char=3]蟲遣いは明らかに愉しんでいる。
警策一本で、部屋中に集まった何万という虫を払う事などできない。
臓硯が号令を下せば、何をやっても虫の波に飲まれるだろう。
pages.en:
…Zouken, master of the swarm, is plainly enjoying himself.

I cannot drive away tens of thousands of insects with one admonition stick.

At Zouken’s command, the tide will swallow me regardless of what I attempt.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…It’s obvious that he is enjoying this.
I can’t fight off thousands of worms with just this stick.
I’ll be swallowed in those worms once Zouken gives the order.

pages.ja:
いや、それとも。
全力で外に逃げ出せば窮地は脱せるかもしれない。
多いといっても所詮は虫だ。
そんな、秒単位で人間一人をどうにかできるとは思えない。
pages.jaRuby:
いや、それとも。
全力で外に逃げ出せば窮地は脱せるかもしれない。
多いといっても所詮は虫だ。
そんな、秒単位で人間一人をどうにかできるとは思えない。
pages.en:
—No. Perhaps—

If I flee at full speed, I may escape this predicament.

However numerous they are, they remain only insects.

I cannot imagine mere insects destroying a human being in a matter of seconds.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Or maybe…
I might be able to escape if I sprint for the exit.
They are just worms, even if it is a horde of them.
It should take them more than a few seconds to kill a human being.

pages.ja:
「よいぞ、ワシは幾らでも待とう。
セイバーの帰還を信じて待ち続けるか、その武器でワシを仕留めるか、それとも我が蟲どもを振り払い外に出るか。好きな死に方を選ぶがよい」
pages.jaRuby:
「よいぞ、ワシは幾らでも待とう。
セイバーの帰還を信じて待ち続けるか、その武器でワシを仕留めるか、それとも我が蟲どもを振り払い外に出るか。好きな死に方を選ぶがよい」
pages.en:
“Take your time. I am willing to wait.

“Remain here and place your faith in Saber’s return. Attempt to kill me with that weapon. Or force your way through my insects and escape outside. Choose whichever death pleases you.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“All right, I shall wait as long as you want.
You can believe in Saber’s return and wait here, try to kill me with that weapon of yours, or shake off my worms and try to escape outside. You can choose how you want to die.”

pages.ja:
……ふん。
どうしたってここから逃がす気はないらしい。
ここで睨み合っていても、周りの虫が増えていくだけだ。
なら

Whatever I choose, he plainly has no intention of letting me leave.

If I continue this standoff, the insects around me will only multiply.

Then—
pages.mirrorMoon:

It seems he has no intention of letting me go.
The worms increase in number as we stand here glaring at one another.
